newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia unemployment rate rose in June - poll.
newsitem.headline: Australia unemployment rate rose in June - poll.

text.p: Australia's unemployment rate rose 0.6 percentage points in June to an unadjusted 9.4 percent and was 0.2 percentage points higher than a year earlier, according to a poll released on Monday.
The Bulletin newsweekly's Morgan poll estimated the number of Australians looking for work rose 51,000 in June to 824,000 and was 24,000 higher than a year earlier.
But it cautioned the estimates were not seasonally adjusted.
The poll also showed that the total workforce rose 12,000 in June to 8.802 million and was 86,000 higher than a year earlier.
The number of employed people fell 39,000 to 7.978 million in June, up 62,000 from June 1996.
While the number of Australians working full-time rose 8,000 to 5.769 million in June, the number of part-time workers fell 48,000 to 2.209 million.
Australians seeking full-time work in June rose 57,000 to 594,000, compared with part-time job seekers falling 6,000 to 230,000.
The unemployment estimates were based on personal interviews of 8,354 Australians aged 14 years and over across Australia during June.
Official June labour force data are due this Thursday. Australia's official unemployment rate was 8.8 percent in May.
